hook: Listen to a midnight radio scene and catch what the voices reveal through tone, hesitation and a surprise at the door.
intro: A radio-play scene with a narrator and two voices: shortly after midnight a knock at the door of a remote forester's lodge, a stranger soaked by the rain, a woman alone with the chain on the door, her hesitation, his polite retreat, her change of heart — and a recognition that turns the scene: the stranger is her former teacher. Literary listening asks less for facts than for atmosphere, motive, reaction and implication: why she hesitates, what her „doch“ reveals, what finally makes her open the door, and how the ending is framed. The narrator's lines supply the reasons and the images; the dialogue supplies tone. Keep the order of events straight — the recognition comes only after she has decided to let him in.
tips[0].title: Scene – tension – reason – turn – resolution
tips[0].text: Time and place → the disturbance (the knock) → hesitation and its reason → the stranger's explanation → the turn (trembling hands, shame) → the surprise (recognition) → an open ending. Questions follow this arc; distractors often borrow a detail from the wrong stage.
tips[0].trap: The recognition comes after her decision. "Sie erkennt ihren Lehrer" is a detail from the wrong stage when the question asks why she lets him in.
tips[0].check.why: Being alone is why she hesitates; the recognition comes only later. The reason for opening is the turn: she sees he is freezing.

tips[1].title: Small words carry the implication
tips[1].text: Particles and politeness formulas are the tone of a radio play: doch signals contradiction and surprise; Verzeihen Sie … and Dann will ich Sie nicht länger aufhalten show a man who does not push. "Was drückt sie aus?" is answered by the particle, not the facts.
tips[1].check.why: doch contradicts what the other person just said: she knows something that does not fit his story.
tips[2].title: Similes are the narrator's, not the facts
tips[2].text: als müsse er … describes how something looks, not what exists. The class photo is an image, not a photo he owns. Check whether a detail belongs to the story world or only to a comparison.
tips[2].check.why: als hätte … introduces an image of how she looks, not something that happens in the story.
remember[0]: Knock – hesitation (why) – explanation – turn (why) – recognition – open ending: keep the stages apart.
remember[1]: Particles (doch) and polite formulas carry tone; als müsse … is an image, not a fact.
exam: Short scenes where atmosphere and motive matter more than facts are typical C1 exam listening — and what radio drama and film ask of you.
tips[0].check.q: 'Es klopft. Sie zögert, denn sie ist allein im Haus. Dann sieht sie, dass er friert, und öffnet. Erst später erkennt sie ihn.' Why does she open the door?
tips[0].check.options[0]: Because she sees he is freezing
tips[0].check.answer: Because she sees he is freezing
tips[1].check.q: 'Sie wollen den letzten Zug nehmen? Der fährt doch nachts gar nicht mehr.' What does doch express here?
tips[1].check.options[0]: Surprise and a hint of doubt about his story
tips[1].check.answer: Surprise and a hint of doubt about his story
tips[2].check.q: The narrator says: 'Sie lächelt, als hätte sie gerade einen alten Brief wiedergefunden.' Does she find a letter in the scene?
tips[2].check.options[0]: No, the letter is only a comparison
tips[2].check.options[1]: Yes, she finds an old letter
tips[2].check.options[2]: Yes, he gives her a letter
tips[2].check.answer: No, the letter is only a comparison
